summary:
I revised the intersection-literature audit to fix every issue from review round 1: 3 major, 4 minor and 2 optional. The main answer stands. As of 2026-10-01 I found no prior or concurrent work that chooses among maximal quadratic-free or S-free sets for the best intersection cut. That is an unsuccessful search, not proof of novelty.

What changed:
- **Proposition 2(b) is a known example.** It is Kılınç-Karzan–Yang (KY) Example 4.3 with the coordinates swapped. I withdrew the claims that it was not found and that it shows KY's strict condition cannot be dropped; KY's own Examples 4.3 and 4.5 already show that. Proposition 2(a) is now also cited to KY Example 4.5.
- **Theorem 1(4) is downgraded.** It is now described as a general sufficient condition for attainment: transversality at every corner minimizer, for S = {q ≤ 0} with any C^1 function q. KY Examples 4.2 and 4.3 already show by example that transversal versus tangential approach decides attainment. Theorem 1(4) does not literally cover their discrete Example 4.2.
- **KY Corollary 3.12 is false as printed.** I refuted it with two exactly checked counterexamples. I stated a corrected form, Cor. 3.12', which requires the ray of each D_2 point to avoid cl(B_2), and showed where KY's proof breaks. Remark 4.4 (deriving Theorem 1(2)) and the Theorem 14 inference now use the corrected form, and the Theorem 14 check gained an exact segment computation.
- **Proposition B now has a general proof**, not just one example F. It uses lineality spaces for the (14a) case and the identity det(S + kJ) = det S + k^2 for the (14b) case.
- **Citation counts.** I reran OpenCitations with the correct Muñoz–Serrano DOI: 7 citers, all already known, so the conclusion is unchanged.
- **Kılınç-Karzan–Steffy (Math. Program. 159, 2016) is added.** I read their author draft; they reprove the cone case of Theorem 1(2) (their Prop. 5) and give a no-assumption result for relaxed cut-generating functions (their Cor. 2) that is close to Theorem 1(5).
- **Solver baseline is weakened.** It now says there is no branch-and-bound comparison "in the sources I could read". The monoidal paper's computations and the Math. Program. 197 version are still inaccessible; Serrano's MIP 2022 slides contain no computations.
- **Proposition A (part 2) is now covered.** For bilinear S its two hypotheses are equivalent, so it applies to none of the corners studied.

A dated "Revision after review round 1" section (Section 14) lists each issue and how it was handled. The revised note has not been re-reviewed.

results.claim: No work found (to 2026-10-01) on choosing among maximal quadratic-free/S-free sets for the best intersection cut or computing the best single intersection cut for QCQP; all citers of the six core papers work on other questions. Unsuccessful search, not proof of novelty.
KY Corollary 3.12 (draft rev. Oct 2017, pp. 17-18) is false as printed: counterexamples are KY Ex. 4.3 with D_1 empty, D_2={(1/2,0)}, and sfree Prop 2(b) with D_2={(1/2,0),(0,1/2)}, A=I, c=(1,1).
Corrected Cor. 3.12' (D_2 points must lie on rays avoiding cl(B_2)) follows from KY Prop. 3.11 by KY's own argument; Prop. 3.11 not verified in every step.
Theorem 1(2) (sup of single-cut bounds = z_K for w>0, including the infinite case) is derivable from Cor. 3.12'; the cone case is in CWY Thm 1.1 and Kilinc-Karzan-Steffy Prop. 5.
Proposition 2(b) of the sfree note is KY Example 4.3 with coordinates swapped (quadratic sublevel set instead of a discrete sequence); Prop 2(a) matches CCDLM Ex. 6.1 variant and KY Ex. 4.5.

Theorem 1(4) is a general sufficient condition (transversality at every minimizer, any C^1 q); KY Ex. 4.2/4.3 illustrate the distinction by example; no general statement found; Ex. 4.2 is not literally covered.

At the Theorem 14 corner the corrected Cor. 3.12' does not apply (the only admissible D_1 point t*-sbar has sigma=1; q(sbar+tau(t*-sbar))=3(1-tau)/2) and KY's necessary conditions are vacuous, while Theorem 1(4) gives attainment.

Proposition B: BCM (14a) sets are exactly the orbit sets C_F with F^T a rotation; if F is invertible and not a scalar multiple of a rotation, C_F is no (14a) set; if det F>0, C_F lies in no (14b) set.
Proposition A applies to none of the 120 McCormick corners: cone(P)=R^3 holds in 0/47 and 0/73 (LP test, tolerance 1e-9), and for bilinear S part (2) is equivalent to part (1).
OpenCitations with the correct Munoz-Serrano 2022 DOI 10.1007/s10107-021-01738-8 gives 7 citers, all already known.
SCIP baseline: no branch-and-bound comparison of quadratic intersection cuts in the sources I could read; the monoidal paper's computations and the Math. Program. 197 version were not accessible.

cd code && OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python3 check_ky_gap_thm14.py > ../logs/check_ky_gap_thm14.log  (lambda=(1/2,1/2,0), q(t*+eps n)=18eps(-60eps-11), new q(sbar+tau(t*-sbar))=3/2-3tau/2, grad.(sbar-t*)=3/2)
cd code && OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python3 check_ky_cor312_counterexample.py > ../logs/check_ky_cor312_counterexample.log  (both counterexamples confirmed exactly)
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 python3 cone_span_mccormick.py 11 150 4 4 3 and 12 200 6 8 4; cmp against existing logs: byte-identical (n=47 and 73, 0 spanning)
curl download + pdftotext + sha256sum of Kilinc-Karzan-Steffy author draft and Serrano MIP 2022 slides (manifest addendum)
grep/awk page-break locators in sources/kilinc-yang2015-sufficiency-draft.txt (Prop 3.11 p.15, Cor 3.12 pp.17-18, Ex 4.2 p.21, Ex 4.3 p.22, Ex 4.5 p.23)
corrections_to_earlier_notes: Round-0 version of this note: claims 'Prop 2(b) shows KY's strict inequality cannot be dropped' and 'Prop 2(b) not found as an example' withdrawn; Prop 2(b) is KY Ex. 4.3 with coordinates swapped.
Round-0 version: Remark 4.4 used KY Cor. 3.12 'as stated'; the printed corollary is false and the argument now uses the corrected Cor. 3.12'.
Round-0 version: Proposition B's general (14a)/(14b) claim was supported by one witness only; now proved in general.
Round-0 version: OpenCitations query used the mistyped DOI 10.1007/s10107-021-01738-x; rerun with -8 (7 citers, nothing new).
Round-0 version: KY Prop. 3.11 locator p. 14 corrected to p. 15.
sfree note Section 10.2: 'the examples of Proposition 2 are elementary; I did not find them stated' is wrong for Prop 2(b) (KY Ex. 4.3) and Prop 2(a) (CCDLM Ex. 6.1 variant, KY Ex. 4.5).
sfree note Theorem 1 Remark (ii): Kilinc-Karzan-Steffy (Math. Program. 159, 2016) Prop. 5 and Cor. 2 should be cited for the cone case and the relaxed-CGF closure result.
open_questions: A characterization of attainment in the equality case that unifies Theorem 1(4) and KY's corrected strict conditions (is tangential approach the only obstruction for quadratics?).
Does a later version of the KY draft correct Cor. 3.12, and is every step of KY Prop. 3.11 correct?
Do the Math. Program. versions of Chmiela et al. (2023) and the monoidal paper (2025) contain branch-and-bound comparisons? Needs library access.
Does the Eckstein-Nediak deepest-cut formulation give a computational route to z_K-attaining maximal quadratic-free sets beyond the orbit family?
Does BCM's violation-maximizing lambda lose a factor against the best orbit member on implied-minor corners (minor-sets stream)?
solver_relevance: Limited. In SCIP 10.0.3 quadratic intersection cuts are off by default. The published reason is cut density and the lack of a rule for when the cuts help, not cut weakness. The only published evaluation I could read measures root-node gap closed (ZIB 20-29: 0.56 versus 0.62), with no branch-and-bound comparison in the accessible sources. The audit's results concern cut strength and novelty, not solver performance. Proposition A applies to none of the LP corners studied.
